questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT part of a basic pre-trip inspection?
questions.explanation: A pre-trip inspection covers safety-critical items such as tires, lights, fluids, and mirrors.

questions.questionText: You should adjust your seat and mirrors before driving, never while driving.
questions.explanation: Adjusting your position while moving takes your eyes and hands off the road.

questions.questionText: Why is good tire tread important?
options: It makes the car look better
It gives grip, especially on wet roads
It reduces fuel needed for the lights
questions.explanation: Tread channels water away and keeps the tires gripping the road, reducing the risk of aquaplaning.

questions.questionText: What should you fasten before starting the engine?
questions.explanation: RA 8750 requires the driver and front passenger to wear seatbelts.

questions.questionText: If your windshield is fogged or dirty and limits your view, you should...
options: Drive slowly and wipe it with your hand
Stop safely and clean it before driving
Keep driving; it will clear on its own
Turn off your wipers and headlights
questions.explanation: A clear view is essential. Never drive with an obstructed windshield.

questions.questionText: What does a steady RED traffic light mean?
options: Stop completely before the stop line
Speed up to clear the intersection
questions.explanation: A steady red light means stop. You may only proceed when directed by a traffic enforcer.

questions.questionText: The light turns AMBER (yellow) as you approach the intersection. You should...
options: Accelerate quickly to beat the red light
Stop safely unless you are too close to stop in time
questions.explanation: Amber means prepare to stop. Do not speed up to cross; stop unless you cannot do so safely.

questions.questionText: In the Philippines, you may proceed on a red light only when a traffic enforcer directs you to.
questions.explanation: A red light means stop. An enforcer's signal overrides the traffic light.

questions.questionText: What color of the traffic light means you may go when it is safe?
questions.explanation: Green means proceed, but only after checking that the intersection is clear.

questions.questionText: What does a FLASHING RED light at an intersection mean?
options: Stop, then proceed only when it is safe
Yield to traffic and keep going
The speed limit is in effect
questions.explanation: A flashing red light is treated like a stop sign: come to a full stop, then go when safe.

questions.questionText: In the Philippines, which side of the road do you normally drive on?
questions.explanation: The Philippines follows right-hand traffic, like the United States. Steer on the right.

questions.questionText: When overtaking another vehicle, you should normally pass it on its...
questions.explanation: In right-hand traffic, overtaking is done on the left, where the oncoming lane is visible.

questions.questionText: Two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time. Who has the right of way?
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive together at an uncontrolled intersection, yield to the vehicle on your right.

questions.questionText: You may cross a solid double yellow line to overtake the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: A solid double yellow line means no overtaking or crossing; treat it as a barrier.

questions.questionText: In right-hand traffic, you pass a slow vehicle ahead on which side?
questions.explanation: Overtaking is normally done on the left side in right-hand traffic countries.

questions.questionText: Match each regulatory sign to its meaning.

matchingPairs.meaning: Come to a complete stop at the stop line.

questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell you what you must or must not do; violating them is a traffic offense.

questions.questionText: A STOP sign requires you to...
options: Slow down and continue if the road is clear
Come to a complete stop at the stop line
Only stop if there is traffic
questions.explanation: A STOP sign is absolute: come to a full stop, check for traffic, then proceed.

questions.questionText: A circular sign with a red border and a black symbol is generally a...
questions.explanation: Red-bordered circular signs are regulatory and prohibit or command a specific action.

questions.questionText: A YIELD (Give Way) sign means you must stop only if there is crossing traffic.
questions.explanation: Yield means slow down and give way; stop only when you need to let other vehicles or pedestrians pass.

questions.questionText: What shape is a STOP sign in the Philippines?
questions.explanation: The octagonal stop sign shape is recognized worldwide.

questions.questionText: Match each warning sign to its meaning.

matchingPairs.meaning: The road may be slippery when wet.
Roundabout ahead; yield to traffic already in the circle.

questions.explanation: Warning signs alert you to hazards ahead so you can slow down and be ready.

questions.questionText: What shape are most warning signs in the Philippines?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow diamonds with black symbols or text.

questions.questionText: A yellow diamond sign showing a winding road warns of...
options: Curves or a winding road ahead
questions.explanation: The winding road symbol means sharp curves lie ahead; slow down before you reach them.

questions.questionText: Warning signs are typically yellow with black symbols or text.
questions.explanation: Yellow-and-black is the standard color scheme for warning signs.

questions.questionText: You see a yellow diamond sign showing a person with a shovel. This warns you to...
options: Speed up to clear the area
Watch for road construction workers and slow down
questions.explanation: This is a men-at-work sign: expect workers and equipment and slow down.

questions.questionText: Blue guide signs in the Philippines typically show...
questions.explanation: Blue signs give directions, route information, and distances to destinations.

questions.questionText: A brown sign along a highway usually indicates...
questions.explanation: Brown signs point the way to scenic, cultural, and tourist destinations.

questions.questionText: Green directional signs on expressways show exits and distances.
questions.explanation: Green is the standard color for directional and destination signs.

questions.questionText: A blue sign with a white 'P' means...
questions.explanation: The 'P' symbol on a blue background marks a parking area.

questions.questionText: What color are most destination guide signs on Philippine highways?
questions.explanation: Green with white text is the standard color for direction and guide signs.

questions.questionText: The best way to avoid a collision is to...
options: Drive fast so you spend less time on the road
Expect the unexpected and scan the road ahead
Rely on your horn to warn others
Assume other drivers will follow the rules
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means scanning ahead, anticipating hazards, and giving yourself room to react.

questions.questionText: Defensive driving means being mentally and physically prepared to react to other drivers' mistakes.
questions.explanation: A defensive driver assumes others may err and keeps space and speed to compensate.

questions.questionText: Under normal conditions, how many seconds should you keep behind the vehicle ahead?
questions.explanation: Keep at least a 3-second gap so you have time to react if the vehicle ahead stops suddenly.

questions.questionText: The brake lights of the vehicle ahead suddenly flash on. Your first reaction should be to...
options: Reduce speed and increase your following distance
questions.explanation: Backing off gives you time and space to handle whatever is causing the slowdown.

questions.questionText: What do you call the area around your vehicle that your mirrors cannot see?
questions.explanation: Blind spots hide vehicles from your mirrors; always glance over your shoulder before changing lanes.

questions.questionText: The usual maximum speed limit for passenger vehicles on Philippine expressways is...
questions.explanation: Most expressways set a 100 km/h maximum for passenger vehicles; always follow the posted limit.

questions.questionText: A speed limit sign applies to...
options: All motor vehicles unless otherwise posted
questions.explanation: Posted speed limits apply to all motor vehicles on that road unless a different limit is posted.

questions.questionText: Doubling your speed roughly quadruples your stopping distance.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance grows with the square of speed, so higher speed needs far more room to stop.

questions.questionText: In wet or rainy weather, you should...
options: Increase your following distance and reduce speed
questions.explanation: Wet roads reduce grip and lengthen stopping distance, so slow down and leave more space.

questions.questionText: What is the common speed limit in Philippine school zones?
questions.explanation: School zones are typically limited to 20 km/h to protect children.

questions.questionText: When driving behind a motorcycle, you should...
options: Follow it very closely to pass quickly
Give it extra space and pass carefully
Overtake it using the same lane
Honk repeatedly until it moves aside
questions.explanation: Motorcycles brake and maneuver faster than cars; give them extra room.

questions.questionText: A jeepney ahead is slowing to pick up passengers. You should...
options: Speed up and pass it on the right
Be patient, watch for pedestrians, and pass only when safe
Squeeze through the gap beside it
Follow it closely until it stops
questions.explanation: Public utility vehicles stop suddenly for passengers; expect people to step out from behind them.

questions.questionText: Pedestrians crossing at a designated crosswalk have the right of way.
questions.explanation: Always stop for pedestrians in a crosswalk, especially near schools and terminals.

questions.questionText: A school bus stops to load or unload students. You should...
options: Pass it as quickly as possible
Slow down and be alert for children crossing
Honk and continue at the same speed
questions.explanation: Children may dart across the road; slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.questionText: What do you call a person traveling on foot?
questions.explanation: Pedestrians are road users too; always yield to them at crossings.

questions.questionText: RA 4136 is commonly known as the...
options: Child Safety in Motor Vehicles Act
questions.explanation: RA 4136, the Land Transportation and Traffic Code of 1964, is the core law on Philippine road traffic.

questions.questionText: Who is required to carry a valid driver's license while driving?
options: Every driver operating a motor vehicle
No one, if the vehicle is owned
questions.explanation: Every motor vehicle driver must carry a valid license and present it when asked by law enforcement.

questions.questionText: A driver involved in a collision must stop, render aid, and report the accident.
questions.explanation: Leaving the scene of an accident you were involved in is a serious offense under RA 4136.

questions.questionText: RA 4136 regulates motor vehicle operation, including the issuance of...
questions.explanation: The law governs licensing of drivers and registration of motor vehicles.

questions.questionText: What agency issues driver's licenses and enforces RA 4136 in the Philippines?
questions.explanation: The Land Transportation Office (LTO) handles licensing and motor vehicle registration.

questions.questionText: RA 10913 (Anti-Distracted Driving Act) prohibits...
options: Using mobile phones and electronic devices while driving
questions.explanation: The law bans using phones and other devices to call, text, or browse while the vehicle is in motion.

questions.questionText: Under RA 10586, the blood alcohol concentration limit for drivers of private vehicles is...
questions.explanation: RA 10586 sets a per se limit of 0.05% BAC for private vehicles and 0.01% for public utility vehicles.

questions.questionText: Under the Anti-Distracted Driving Act, you may use your phone while stopped at a red light.
questions.explanation: The prohibition applies even when the vehicle is temporarily stopped on the road.

questions.questionText: Driving while under the influence of illegal drugs is penalized under...
questions.explanation: RA 9165, the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act, covers drug-related offenses, including DUI.

questions.questionText: The blood alcohol limit for drivers of public utility vehicles under RA 10586 is...
questions.explanation: A stricter 0.01% limit applies to commercial and public utility vehicle drivers.

questions.questionText: Under RA 10930, a new driver's license is valid for how many years?
questions.explanation: Licenses are issued for 5 years and may be renewed for 10 years if the driver has no recorded violations.

questions.questionText: What is the minimum age to apply for a student permit in the Philippines?
questions.explanation: You may apply for a student permit at 16; a non-professional license requires being at least 17.

questions.questionText: Accumulating demerit points for traffic violations can lead to license suspension or revocation.
questions.explanation: The demerit point system tracks violations; too many points within two years can suspend your license.

questions.questionText: A non-professional driver's license allows you to...
options: Drive any motor vehicle without restrictions
Drive vehicles for personal or household use
Operate a taxi or bus for hire
questions.explanation: Non-professional licenses cover personal driving; driving for hire needs a professional license.

questions.questionText: What system records penalty points against a driver for traffic violations?
questions.explanation: The demerit point system assigns points per violation; reaching the threshold within two years brings penalties.
